title: THERMOMECHANICAL BEHAVIOR OF SOLID OXIDE CELLS
subtitle: Thermal mismatch, residual stress, and multilayer mechanics in electrochemical cells.
image_alt: Illustrative colored stress field across layered ceramic materials
summary: Layered electrochemical cells experience different thermal strains across electrodes and electrolytes. Modeling the resulting mechanical constraints helps identify stress concentrations and potential failure locations.
question: How do thermal expansion mismatch, layer thickness, and interfaces shape the stress state in a multilayer solid oxide cell?
approach: Represent the cell as a layered continuum with material-dependent elastic and thermal properties.
Apply thermal loading and appropriate mechanical constraints; solve the coupled displacement equilibrium problem.
Compare stress distributions in the electrolyte, electrode support, and regions near interfaces.
deliverables: Replace the illustrative artwork with a validated temperature map, stress contours, and a layer-by-layer stress comparison.

title: PHASE-FIELD SIMULATION OF BRITTLE FRACTURE
subtitle: Nonlinear mechanics, damage evolution, and numerical convergence for fracture.
image_alt: Illustrative diffuse damage band and crack propagating through a numerical mesh
summary: A regularized phase-field variable represents the transition from intact material to cracked material. Combining this damage field with mechanical equilibrium allows complex crack paths to emerge without explicit crack tracking.
question: How can a crack path be resolved while retaining a stable and interpretable nonlinear solution process?
approach: Discretize displacement and phase-field variables and assemble the coupled weak-form equations.
Use incremental loading with alternate minimization or staggered mechanics–damage updates.
Examine energy evolution, convergence behavior, load-step cutbacks, and mesh sensitivity.
deliverables: Add your crack-evolution frames, load–displacement curve, energy history, and solver convergence plots.

title: FFT-BASED COMPUTATIONAL MECHANICS
subtitle: Spectral discretization and iterative field solvers for spatially varying materials.
image_alt: Illustrative spectral wave field and periodic grid
summary: Spectral discretizations offer an alternative route to field solutions on regular grids. They are especially useful when exploring heterogeneous material responses and the impact of iterative solver choices.
question: What can frequency-domain operators reveal about efficiency and field resolution in heterogeneous mechanics problems?
approach: Represent heterogeneous material properties on a regular numerical grid.
Evaluate field operators in Fourier space and iterate until the governing residual is controlled.
Compare computed strain or stress fields and convergence histories against suitable reference cases.
deliverables: Replace the schematic with your actual heterogeneous microstructure, computed response field, and solver benchmarks.
